players.product: E-Infrastructure site development (earthwork, grading, site utilities) and CEC electrical construction for hyperscale data-center and semiconductor campuses

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CEO): revenue growth of 92% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 120%; adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, with margins expanding over 150 basis points YoY to a first-quarter record of 20%. Operating cash flow was $166 million. Management said it is pursuing the projects with the best returns: 'We're not looking to win all projects. We are looking to win the best projects.'
quarterly_data.figure: revenue growth of 92%; adjusted diluted EPS growth of 120%; adjusted EBITDA margin 20% (over 150 basis points expansion); operating cash flow $166 million

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog at end of Q1 2026 (CEO/CFO): signed backlog $3.8 billion (a 78% YoY increase, or 51% excluding CEC); combined backlog (signed plus unsigned awards) $5.2 billion (up 131%, or 46% excluding CEC). High-probability future-phase opportunities total over $1.3 billion, so the total pool of work is approaching $6.5 billion, grown by approximately $2 billion since year-end. Q1 book-to-burn ratios were 2.1x for backlog and 3.5x for combined backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: signed backlog $3.8 billion (78%); combined backlog $5.2 billion (131%); future phase over $1.3 billion; total pool approaching $6.5 billion; book-to-burn 2.1x / 3.5x

quarterly_data.signal: E-Infrastructure Q1 2026: revenue grew 174% (organic growth of over 100%), with the data center market again the primary growth driver; adjusted operating income increased 177% as margins expanded despite the dilutive CEC acquisition; site development revenue more than doubled. CEC (electrical) delivered 78% revenue growth vs its prior-year Q1, and several large CEC project wins in the quarter contributed to a $1.2 billion increase in CEC combined backlog since year-end 2025; the Texas market 'remains exceptionally strong with robust award activity in early 2026'. E-Infrastructure signed backlog + unsigned electrical awards + future-phase site development opportunities now exceeds $5 billion; mission-critical work (data centers, large manufacturing, semiconductor) was over 90% of E-Infrastructure signed backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: E-Infrastructure revenue 174% growth (organic over 100%); adjusted operating income 177%; CEC revenue growth 78%; CEC combined backlog $1.2 billion increase since year-end; E-Infrastructure pool exceeds $5 billion; mission-critical over 90% of signed backlog

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised on the Q1 call (CFO): revenue $3.7 billion-$3.8 billion (midpoint a 20% increase over previous guidance, more than 50% growth over 2025); diluted EPS $16.50-$17.15; adjusted diluted EPS $18.40-$19.05 (midpoint a 36% increase from previous guidance, 72% growth over 2025); EBITDA $801 million-$831 million; adjusted EBITDA $843 million-$873 million. CEO: E-Infrastructure revenue growth of 80% or higher including full-year CEC, legacy business growing at rates approaching 60% or higher, E-Infrastructure adjusted operating margins in the mid 20% range. CapEx forecast $100 million-$110 million, unchanged. Point-in-time guidance, raised again on the Q2 call.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.7 billion-$3.8 billion; adjusted diluted EPS $18.40-$19.05; adjusted EBITDA $843 million-$873 million; E-Infrastructure revenue growth of 80% or higher; E-Infrastructure margins mid 20% range

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor: during Q1 Sterling was awarded the first phase of a multi-phase semiconductor fabrication campus (customer not named) as site development partner for a mega fab; the first phase is executed under a joint venture by its union Petillo operation in the Northeast, totals over $500 million and is expected to be completed in late 2027 or early 2028, with the campus build spanning a multi-decade period. CEO: 'It's the biggest semi fab plant in the U.S.' and 'the first semiconductor project we've done'; he does not see 'the huge rush of chip plants coming out till 2029, 2030' and expects Sterling to be 'the supplier of choice for every chip plant that comes out in the future.' Other large manufacturing projects could be awarded in 2026 or early 2027 with similar margin profiles.
quarterly_data.figure: first phase over $500 million; completion late 2027 or early 2028; chip-plant wave 2029, 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Hyperscaler demand and geography (CEO): data-center projects are now 'north of 1,000 acres, and the future projects coming out look like they're multi-thousand acres'; a typical project today is about three years, the coming ones 'four and five year projects', and key customers are already discussing projects starting 2028, 2029. Customers are pulling Sterling into new geographies including Texas, the Pacific Northwest and the Midwest; 'we've let the major hyperscalers pull us into new markets... They're kind of screaming to get into these markets faster with what they see coming in capital spending they're going to do.' Sterling is turning down smaller work, and margin gains come from vertical integration and execution, not price: 'Everybody keeps asking us if we're getting more price. The answer is no, we're not getting more price.' New Pacific Northwest projects are expected in 2027, 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: projects north of 1,000 acres; typical project three years, coming ones four and five year projects

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and CEC cross-selling (CEO): joint site-development plus electrical awards materialized six to eight months ahead of expectations, with two data center projects in active construction using both services. CEC margin expansion of 300 to 500 basis points expected in 12 to 18 months as low-margin end markets are exited. Sterling locked down a lease to triple the size of its modular build capabilities and may expand modular to other U.S. locations over the next 18 months. Labor is the constraint: 'I just wish I had 2,000 or 3,000 more electricians, and we would grow it even faster.' A typical internal electrical package is $300 million-$500 million, released in phases. An internal AI project added about 15% project-manager capacity; the equipment rental and lease market is 'extremely tight'.
quarterly_data.figure: joint awards six to eight months early; CEC margin 300 to 500 basis points in 12 to 18 months; lease to triple modular build capabilities; internal electrical package $300 million-$500 million

contracts.signal: CEO: 'We started with a pilot with Meta, as a matter of fact, who asked us to go to the upper Northwest, Pacific Northwest.' Sterling used yellow iron and assets from its Utah highway business with Atlanta project-management teams. The CEO said the Pacific Northwest work 'we started two years ago' and 'We've got multiple through there'; the teams got 'five or six projects out of that between the customers and the GCs' (that count is not attributed to Meta alone).
contracts.date_signed: started two years ago (per the 05-05-2026 call)
